column1: # Owner decisions of recipe qualification/residency-pressure-alloc-20261107 (RESIDENCY_PRESSURE_ALLOC v1), written before the edit. Debt: #2653 (residency fold leaf PS) GATES.tsv allocation_jit open item: PRESSURE_AWARE resident use() allocated 48 B/call in 2 of 8 JIT runs (C2 does not always scalar-replace the HeapSnapshot built inside targetBudget), always under -Xint, and 0 -> 48 in one -Xbatch JVM (fixed budget, then PRESSURE_AWARE). M3JDK master 6f495787649; owner jdk.m3.collections.M3ObjectResidency (preimage blob b8793d63a3cd = #2653's postimage).

column2: where does the per-call object come from
column3: HeapSnapshot.current() inside targetBudget(), read for one field (estimatedHeadroomBytes) at every PRESSURE_AWARE boundary: admission, enforceBudget (the resident use() hit path and signalMemoryPressure), both reuse budget checks
column4: the record is the only allocation on the PRESSURE_AWARE resident hit path
column5: -Xint probe on master: pressure_aware signalMemoryPressure, resident_use, refused_reuse and admission_net_of_decision 48 B/call each; fixed_budget 0 (no snapshot since #2653)

column3: (a) one HeapSnapshot per residency, reused; (b) a mutable snapshot type owned by the residency
column5: HeapSnapshot is a public record (immutable, public API): reuse cannot refresh it; a second mutable snapshot type would be a second owner of the same three heap reads for one long

column2: cache the sample (sampled-at epoch + cached budget)
column3: refresh the cached budget every N boundaries or every T nanoseconds
column5: between refreshes a boundary would see a stale budget: PRESSURE_AWARE budgets and victims could differ from #2653 under a moving heap (the debt requires the same budgets and victims); D4 removes the object without any cache, so no epoch is needed

column3: private static long sampledHeadroomBytes(): Runtime.totalMemory(), freeMemory(), maxMemory() in HeapSnapshot.current()'s order, used = max(0, committed - free), headroom = max(0, max - used); targetBudget() subtracts the reserve and caps the maximum exactly as before
column5: no object exists on any path, so the figure no longer depends on inlining or escape analysis; HeapSnapshot.current() reads maxMemory() twice (maxBytes and the headroom), the primitive reads it once: maxMemory() is the fixed maximum heap capacity of the running JVM, so the values are the same; every boundary still samples the running heap at the same points in the same order
HeapSnapshot stays public API, unchanged (M3ObjectResidency$HeapSnapshot.class byte-identical); the private method restates its headroom arithmetic for the budget only

column2: other owners of the heap reads
column3: jdk.m3.collections.M3RuntimeHeap (protected: API use only), M3MemoryPressure (#2658; the paged array's probe seam), M3HeapGrowth (growth sampler)
column5: M3RuntimeHeap and M3MemoryPressure return records/objects per sample (the allocation this leaf removes); M3HeapGrowth samples used bytes without the clamps targetBudget needs; #2658's RELOCATION_MAP NEC row already records the shared Runtime reads

column3: M3ObjectResidency only (targetBudget body + one private static method); one new JUnit class
column5: M3TransientFacadeStore, the hash/tree maps, M3Filtered*, the rank family, M3IndexPathMasks, M3Signal*/M3ObjectSignal*, primitives and the mat owners are untouched (class files byte-identical, GATES.tsv untouched_classes)
